page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Signature mark at bottom left. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: dem δήμοις[?], credo secundum tribuum numerum. Hi ad difquisitionem actorum magistratus omnes potestate decedentes vocabant, & velitatione apud se instituta præjudicio suo aut damnabant eos, aut absolvebant, interdum etiam incertos demittebant, aut populo proponebant, populusq; obiter & perfunctorie recognitâ, quid sibi videretur, declarabat, sed sententiam definitivam, quâ standum esset, nō ferebat, totû vero hoc ex veteri lege judicibus permittebat.

Logistæ post hæc quasi præludia ad judices Heliastas ex officio eosdem hos introducebant, ut ii cognitione integrâ susceptâ inquirerent accuratius in ea, de quibus forte infimularentur introducti: & simul voce publicâ præconis ad dicendum invitabant quosvis, si qui essent, quibus accusare introductos luberet.

Nec ferè deerant, (quomodo enim deesse poterant æmuli in civitate dissensionum & simultatum plena?) qui meditatâ jam ante orationem in eos dicerent. Tum audità utráque parte (nam defendendi sui copia accusatis non negabatur) heliastæ sententiam ferebant, cui parendum erat. Et fiebat nonnun-quàm, ut quos populus, aut λογισταὶ[?] præjudicio suo damnaverant, judices absolverent, aut absolutos ab istis da-

page.notes: Top right of the page the printed number is 89. The running head reads REIP. ATHENIENSIVM. The first word "dem" is a fragment of a Greek word ending in -οις; the Greek letters are uncertain, hence [?]. "λογισταὶ" in the last paragraph is also uncertain. Parts of the word "da-" at the end continue on the next page. Faint marks at the bottom right (a partial "F" and "613"-like stamp or show-through) are not printed text on this page and are left out. Long s and ligatures (st, ft) are transcribed as plain s and st.
